posts.title: Shakira Sets Amazon Music Livestream Record With Madrid Show and Dua Lipa Duet
posts.excerpt: Shakira's October 3 Madrid concert became Amazon Music's most-viewed livestream by a female artist.
posts.body:
Shakira's October 3 Madrid concert became Amazon Music's most-viewed livestream by a female artist. Dua Lipa appeared during the show for a surprise performance of "Antología," and Amazon announced the streaming record the following day without publishing a viewer total.

The show streamed worldwide through Amazon Music, Prime Video and Twitch and marked Shakira's first full-concert global livestream. Amazon's claim applies specifically to its own platform, not to concert streams across every service. The performance took place at Shakira Stadium, a temporary venue built inside Madrid's Iberdrola Music complex for the residency, with capacity for more than 50,000 people. The broadcast was part of Amazon Music's 2026 Women Shaping Latin Music campaign. The surprise duet also reached back to *Pies Descalzos*, where "Antología" first appeared in 1995.

[ig:p:DeFRhLolil0|@shakira|https://www.instagram.com/p/DeFRhLolil0/]

Dua had already covered "Antología" at her own Bogotá show in 2025 while Shakira was performing the same song that night in Asunción. The two later exchanged messages of admiration online, but they had never performed together. In Madrid, Shakira introduced Dua by saying she admired her and considered herself a fan before the two sang the song together for the first time onstage.

The residency sits inside Es Latina, a month-long cultural program built around Macondo Park. The temporary city takes its name from Gabriel García Márquez's fictional Macondo and was designed as part of the concert site rather than as a separate event elsewhere in Madrid. Macondo Park includes a Shakira museum, a literature area, food and fashion spaces, and additional live performances around the main concerts.

posts.title: Frequency Of Love
posts.excerpt: Victoria Monét has released her second album *Frequency Of Love*, a 22-song record that moves between R&B, house, funk and acoustic soul.
posts.body:
Victoria Monét has released her second album *Frequency Of Love*, a 22-song record that moves between R&B, house, funk and acoustic soul. Released October 2, it is her first full-length since *JAGUAR II*, which won Best R&B Album as Monét took Best New Artist at the 2024 Grammys.

The gap was deliberate. Monét has said she wanted enough life to happen before making the next record, and part of that time took her to culinary school. She graduated from the Institute of Culinary Education in May 2026 and completed an externship at Verse L.A. while rehearsing for Bruno Mars' European stadium tour. Cooking gave her a way to make something without immediately turning it into promotion or income after the long Grammy cycle around *JAGUAR II*.

*Frequency Of Love* began with a narrower idea. Monét was tracing musicians who worked on records by Michael Jackson and Quincy Jones, which led her toward Toto and yacht rock. Culinary school disrupted that plan in a useful way. On pasta days she listened to Italian artists, and when the class made Jamaican food she listened to Jamaican records. The final album keeps some of that influence but moves well beyond it.

"Reach Out" leans into house, "You Hurt Me Too" was written with a James Bond theme in mind, and "Juicy" carries more of the album's early concept. "Reach Out" also predates the album. Monét recorded it around the period when the *JAGUAR II* deluxe edition was being assembled, then held it back because she thought it deserved more than a bonus-track slot. Its video was shot at the Salk Institute in La Jolla.

[youtube:h99lQg2zSl0]

Monét has described love on the album broadly, including romance, heartbreak, self-love and motherhood. Her daughter Hazel Monét appears with Leon Thomas on "You Mean The World To Me." Elsewhere, the songs move between attraction, disappointment and the risk that comes with letting someone close.

The album also reaches back to "Somebody," a mid-century standard Monét first heard as a child while watching *Introducing Dorothy Dandridge* with her grandmother. Dandridge stayed with her long enough that Monét later dressed as her for Halloween twice.

Monét takes *Frequency Of Love* on a 27-city North American tour beginning October 27 in Raleigh. She is also launching the Frequency Of Love Foundation, which plans youth programs around food, agriculture, cooking and wellness. Its first plans include hands-on food education and community gardens.
